mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 6 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI growth and subsequent 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE and subsequent 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous 3 months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the previous 6 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and profitability.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and subsequent 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS monthly change and subsequent 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% year-over-year, it signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and subsequent 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is growing at an annual rate above 3%, the combination signals tightening monetary conditions and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on subsequent 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth is negative and real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% year-over-year, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO 6-month growth < 0 AND GDPC1 YoY growth < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 on subsequent 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
